title: Canonical affine localization of a fine fan at a point
statement:
Let $(F,\mathcal P_F)$ be a fine fan, with fine and sharp monoids, local monoidal-space morphisms, monoid spectra and sharpening as in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], and let $z\in F$. Put $P=\mathcal P_{F,z}$ and let $F_z$ be the set of generalizations of $z$. Then $F_z$ is the smallest open neighborhood of $z$, $P$ is a fine sharp monoid, and there is a canonical isomorphism of fans
$$\iota_z:(F_z,\mathcal P_F|_{F_z})\xrightarrow{\sim}S(P)=(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P,\overline{\widetilde P}).$$
The germ homomorphism $\Gamma(F_z,\mathcal P_F)\to P$ is an isomorphism, and its composite with pullback of the canonical section $p$ along $\iota_z$ is $p$ for every $p\in P$. More explicitly, in any affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}A$ containing $z$, let $\mathfrak p$ represent $z$, choose a finite generating tuple $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $A$, and put $s=\sum_{a_i\notin\mathfrak p}a_i$, with empty sum $0$. In that chart
$$F_z=D(s)=\{\mathfrak q:\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p\},\qquad A[s^{-1}]=A_{\mathfrak p},\qquad P\simeq A_{\mathfrak p}/A_{\mathfrak p}^{\times},$$
and $\iota_z$ is the isomorphism induced by localization and quotient by units, including the sharpened structure sheaves.

proof.text: Choose a fine chart at z. Apply [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood] to a finite generating tuple, pull the smallest basic neighborhood back through the chart homeomorphism and push it along the open inclusion. Any neighborhood of z restricts to a chart neighborhood containing this basic open, proving minimality in the whole fan. Membership is equivalent to specialization to z by the open-neighborhood characterization of Specializes.

The smallest neighborhood U is terminal in the opposite category of open neighborhoods of z. Mathlib isIso_ι_of_isTerminal makes its germ an isomorphism, giving bijectivity without computing sharp sections. Fineness of the actual stalk follows from [lem-trf-fine-fan-chart-stalk-coordinates] in a chosen chart; sharpness is a field of Fan. Restriction preserves sharp stalks by Mathlib restrictStalkIso.

For the chosen chart use [lem-trf-fine-fan-chart-minimal-affine] to construct a local normalized affine-stalk isomorphism iota. Two local normalized isomorphisms have equal canonical-section pullbacks: cancel the injective germ and the global-section transport along an equality of opens. Injectivity in [lem-trf-affine-fan-hom-universal] then identifies their hom morphisms, hence their isomorphisms. This proves uniqueness using normalization alone.

For any chart and any finite generating tuple, use [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood]. Its basic open and U each describe generalizations of the same point, so the chart membership formulas agree. Its intersection formula gives the subset-of-primes equation by contraposition, and its localization equality supplies the third formula. Apply [lem-trf-fine-fan-chart-stalk-coordinates] for the numerator-normalized stalk equivalence. Apply [lem-trf-fine-fan-chart-minimal-affine] again in this chart; uniqueness from Step 3 identifies its isomorphism with iota, and substitution gives the required sheafed-space chart square.

It is a first split with no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the item as created by Q120, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Source checked: ILO VIII 3.1.1–3.1.4(iii) (p.98), 3.1.8(ii) and 3.1.10(ii) (pp.99–100), and the proof of 3.3.15 (p.109, the F′=Spec(M_F,c(y)) paragraph); the statement matches them, and there is no SGA. Steps: Step 1 shows D(s)=∩_{f∉p}D(f)={q⊆p} is the set of generalizations and the smallest neighbourhood in F, via the open chart and minimal-neighborhood. Step 2 shows the germ map A_s→A_p is the identity, from the sections lemma. Step 3 shows B is fine and sharp using integral-sharpening only (no saturation or torsion-freeness). Step 4 builds the extension/contraction homeomorphism; I checked the ambiguity a−ns=a′−n′s via integrality plus primeness. Step 5 gives the prime bijection for the quotient by units. Step 6 gives explicit inverse localized-sharpening maps, well defined because B is integral. Step 7 proves A[(a+s)^{-1}]=Q[t^{-1}] in both directions, and the basis-lemma Mathlib leaf in commutative monoids extends the maps to inverse sheaf isomorphisms. Step 8 shows γ∘ι*=id and gets canonicity from affine-fan-hom-universal, whose hypotheses (sharp stalks, P fine sharp) hold. Small cases checked: A=0, A a group, p=∅, p maximal, N² at a height-one prime, repeated or unit generators, a non-sharp torsion A. No cycle in the 150-node closure, and all cited nodes are in unit sk-i-curve-zero or are a Mathlib leaf. Advisory only: lem-trf-fan-chart-local-monoid-lift and lem-trf-fine-monoid-local-smooth-charts (both unsplit and later) contain this fact as one clause and should cite this item when they are split.
